events_basis.text: N x C / M with N = 0, so 0 events a year. N is the number of distinct marketplace actions that this institution's scheduled workflows run by floating tag. Read at driftwood main 08ba2d0 on 2026-11-15: the one workflow, loop.yml, names one action, actions/checkout, three times, each by the commit 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 and none by tag. C = 2 (min, mode) to 7 (max) marketplace actions with a published compromise in 2025: for the min and the mode, the two that CISA's alert of 2025-03-18 names (tj-actions/changed-files, CVE-2025-30066, and reviewdog/action-setup, CVE-2025-30154); for the max, those two plus the five downstream reviewdog actions Wiz named on 2025-03-17 as compromised through action-setup (action-shellcheck, action-composite-template, action-staticcheck, action-ast-grep, action-typos). M = 23,757 marketplace actions counted over four months (Chaiwut and Nikiforakis, 'Time for Actions: A Longitudinal Study of the GitHub Actions Marketplace', IEEE SecDev 2025). C and M are as read on 2026-09-26 and were not read again. Up to version 5.0.1 this row kept N = 1, read on 2026-09-26 at driftwood 155db9e for one workflow only, twin-sweep.yml, which ran actions/checkout@v4. That gave 8.42e-05 to 0.000295 events a year. Driftwood deleted that workflow on 2026-11-14. The method counts one kind of door only: a marketplace action, run by floating tag, that is compromised at that tag. It does not count any other way a scheduled workflow's write credential could be misused. Nobody has counted those. So 0 is this method's count, not an upper bound on every misuse of that credential.
